scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three” (preprints/Absolutely-Continuous-Spectrum-for-Weak-Disorder-Anderson-Models-in-Dimensions-at-Least-Three-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0d971c56f6ba1641), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a fixed sufficiently small number e2 ∈ (0, 1/100) such that, for every fixed integer d ≥ 3, there is a number λd > 0 with the following property. Set Id = ( (−6 + e2/2, −6 + e2), d = 3, −2d + (1/200, 1/100), d ≥ 4. (2) Then for every fixed 0 < λ < λd, almost surely Id ⊂ σ(Hλ,ω), χId (Hλ,ω)ℓ2 (Zd ) ⊂ Hac(Hλ,ω). In particular, the spectral restriction to Id is purely absolutely continuous and χId (Hλ,ω) ̸= 0. For d ≥ 4, one may take λd = √ 3 2−n∗(d), where the finite-matrix specification of n∗(d) is given in Definition 8.2. For d = 3, the proof supplies an existential positive threshold.
